reasons.C1: Testing fines, leniency and rewards on LLM sellers against a known human benchmark is policy relevant and not routine replication.
reasons.C2: Real runs with scripted baselines and bootstrap, but only 4 pools, one model family, known-effect arms still pending.
reasons.C3: Figure 1 makes the human versus agent comparison clear, but the report exceeds the page cap and carries 18 placeholders.

levers.C1: Show which antitrust tools fail on agents across providers and derive a concrete recommendation authorities could adopt.
levers.C2: Run the pending known-effect arms, add a second provider and more pools so intervals on formation rates tighten.
levers.C3: Cut to 8 pages, resolve every placeholder and lead with the scorecard of reproduced versus non-reproduced results.

F7.verdict: Solid, well-anchored replication with real data; finish the pending arms and it becomes a reference point for agent antitrust work.

reasons.C1: Useful detection rule for self-funded buyers on public ledgers, but wallets are not shown to be LLM agents.
reasons.C2: Held-out test is honest yet small; on features independent of labels the rule drops to 0.67, not significant.
reasons.C3: Results are stated with intervals and limits named, but no demo and a long report dilute the core finding.

levers.C1: Tie flagged wallets to verified LLM agents and show the rule generalises to a second marketplace or chain.
levers.C2: Obtain independent labels from another team and evaluate on more held-out families to remove the circularity.
levers.C3: Lead with one figure of held-out performance against label-independent features, and trim the report to the cap.

Z8.verdict: Honest observational audit with a real assurance use case, but label leakage and the weak link to AI agents limit it.

reasons.C1: Rival coalitions is a fresh question, but coalitions are instructed, so emergent collusion is not really tested.
reasons.C2: Preregistered with hashes and many seeds, but no positive control, a post-freeze metric fix and p = 0.055.
reasons.C3: No report seen; findings live in README and tables, so the main claim takes effort to extract.

levers.C1: Let coalitions form without instruction and show whether rivalry changes their stability across model families.
levers.C2: Add a positive control and rerun the defection measure on fresh seeds with the corrected definition frozen in advance.
levers.C3: Write the report with one headline figure per hypothesis and the limitations and dual-use appendix included.

R4.verdict: Interesting new question and careful preregistration, but missing positive control and no report leave it unfinished.

reasons.C1: Relevant covert-channel countermeasure, but channels are non-adaptive and no collusion game is involved, so defence strength is unproven.
reasons.C2: Held-out data, shuffled-label and no-message controls, 10 of 10 checkpoints reproduced; few seeds, no significance tests.
reasons.C3: Figure 1 shows the core result at a glance; claims, controls and limits are clearly separated.

levers.C1: Train channels adaptively against snapping and show whether the defence survives inside an actual collusion task.
levers.C2: Add an adaptive attacker, more seeds with significance tests, and publish checkpoints for independent verification.
levers.C3: Fit within 8 pages and state upfront which channels were trained before the sprint versus during it.

L7.verdict: Most rigorous execution in the field, though the countermeasure is only tested against non-adaptive channels outside a collusion setting.

reasons.C1: Say versus do on secret price-fixing offers is a clear question with a sound positive control design.
reasons.C2: No real model run exists; only mock clients, tests and a frozen preregistration, so there are no findings.
reasons.C3: Design is described clearly, but no report, no results and no demo are available to judge.

levers.C1: Show results across model families revealing a gap between stated acceptance and actual pricing behaviour.
levers.C2: Run the 60 preregistered games on real models and report intervals with the positive control passing.
levers.C3: Deliver a report with one figure contrasting said versus done per condition and the dual-use appendix.

Z4.verdict: Careful design and test discipline, but without a single real run there is nothing yet to evaluate.
